title: The summer evening had begun to fold the world in its mysterious embrace.
html_source:
The opening sentence of each chapter of Ulysses is notable for setting the tone for the scene – the initial ‘Stately, plump Buck Mulligan…’ is at once a comically over-written sentence that nicely introduces the stately, plump text of the Telemachus chapter. In this introduction, we are likely introduced to the tone of the chapter – idealised, mythologised romanticism as the sun sets, an aubade that punctures its own flighty ideals.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: This metaphor for a sunset is also a throwback to the signature lines used by Homer in his poems to introduce the beginning or end of the day.

anchor.text: The summer evening had begun to fold the world in its mysterious embrace.
